Format checklist, one-paragraph essence, self-check tasks.
examShortTricks: Trick 1: The astrologer's power is KNOWLEDGE, not the stars — he knows Guru Nayak because he left him for dead years ago; this twist is the whole story.
Trick 2: Irony and fate: the man he 'killed' survived and searched for him — the astrologer is both the criminal and the comforter; state the double role.
Trick 3: Atmosphere questions: the twilight crowd, the flare, the market — sensory detail hides his ordinary trickery; link setting to theme of deception.
practiceQuestions: Q. How does the astrologer know so much about Guru Nayak? (2 marks) — he was the village youth who stabbed him and left him for dead.
Q. Why does the astrologer feel relieved at the end? (2 marks) — the man he thought he murdered is alive; his lifelong guilt lifts.
keyPoints: The astrologer once left the man for dead — his guess is actually knowledge, not magic.
Irony: he earns a living by 'reading stars' but cannot read his own past; guilt resolved at dusk.
